text:
maria: Packaging found a checksum mismatch on the airgap submanifest for private-installer v1.9.4-hotpatch. Holding the 10:30 PT delivery window. @deploybot, pause pins and canary promotion.

deploybot: Received pause. All automatic promotions are suspended for manifest id `pkg-priv-1-9-4-hotpatch`.

ryan: Copy. Do we have the mismatched file id? which artifact?

maria: It looks like `installer-v1.9.4-hotpatch.tar.gz` has sha256 A vs expected B in the signed-submanifest. Packaging thinks the pack step re-compressed with different gzip settings.

sneha: Ugh. That would break airgapped installs. If it's just gzip flags, we can rebuild with deterministic gzip. Recommend we regenerate and re-sign.

kaya: Agree. Two quick asks: (1) can we avoid reusing the same artifact name (so customers don't get confused), (2) what's the rollback/escape hatch if regen/sign takes too long?

maria: Regen + re-sign is estimated 18-25 mins. I don't want to push a new name unless we have to. For escape hatch: we can pin previous manifest `pkg-priv-1-9.3.2` as the live deliverable and mark `1.9.4-hotpatch` as aborted. Ops would need to allow backfill in the delivery transport.

ops-bot: Note: pinning previous manifest requires KMS access to release-signing key and a manual override for `deliverbot` transport. ETA for ops on that is ~10m if approved.

ryan: If we pin back, we need to open a rollback ticket and notify CS + security. I can draft the release note: "Abort v1.9.4-hotpatch; republish when deterministic build fixed." Who owns the republish?

sneha: Packaging owns regen/sign. I'll take the republish once packaging confirms deterministic artifact + cosign signature pass locally.

kaya: Ops: approve pin back to `1.9.3.2` as escape hatch? We need a decision by 10:14 PT so deploybot can finish early-stage checks.

ops-bot: Approved by ops lead. Manual override scheduled. Deploybot: hold promotion and mark `pkg-priv-1-9-4-hotpatch` state=aborted in release ledger.

deploybot: Done: promotion held, ledger updated to aborted. Canary seeds untouched. All routes still pointing to `pkg-priv-1-9.3.2` until further notice.

maria: Packaging will rebuild with `--gzip=deterministic` and run `cosign sign` using release KMS. I'll post checksums when done.

sneha: Quick check commands for QA when packaging done:
```
sha256sum installer-v1.9.4-hotpatch.tar.gz
cosign verify-blob --key kms://projects/release/keys/priv-sign ./installer-v1.9.4-hotpatch.tar.gz
```
If both pass, we can re-open the window and pin.

ryan: I'll prepare communication: short note for customers in the delivery channel + internal incident note. Add context: no installs started, canary blocked.

maria: Update: rebuild started (10:07 PT). ETA ~14 mins.

kaya: Thanks. If rebuild finishes before 10:25 PT we will attempt a limited canary (5 seeds) and observe token exchange + install. If anything looks off we abort and keep 1.9.3.2.

sneha: Packaging reporting successful deterministic gzip and cosign OK (10:19 PT). New sha256: B2C3D... full checksum posted below.

maria: Posting checksum: sha256=B2C3D4E5F6A7... (full in vault). Re-sign manifests pushed to release signer. @deploybot you can attempt pin to v1.9.4-hotpatch for canary seeds only.

deploybot: Canary pin request accepted. Promoting `pkg-priv-1-9-4-hotpatch` to 5 seeds starting 10:22 PT. Monitoring hooks enabled.

ops-bot: Reminder: if any seed reports install error exit !=0 within 15m, auto-abort will revert to 1.9.3.2.

ryan: Noted. Draft sent to CS + security. Will update once canary green.

maria: Canary reports 0/5 errors at 10:35 PT, logs look clean. Rolling to staged batch (30% of seeds) at 10:37 PT.

sneha: Packaging to follow up with final signed-submanifest copy and full checksum list for audit.

kaya: Good job. Closing the hold. Final note: we should add deterministic gzip to our CI for future builds to avoid this class of mismatch.

maria: Filing CI ticket after this thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
